title: Internet Message Format

hero.subtitle: Defining the syntax of email messages - headers, body, addresses, and dates - the format behind every email you've ever sent or received.

subtitle: Defining the syntax of email messages - headers, body, addresses, and dates - the format behind every email you've ever sent or received.
summary: RFC 5322 defines what an Internet email message looks like: a block of header fields such as From, To, Date and Subject, a blank line, and then the body. It says nothing about how a message is delivered, which is the job of SMTP. It replaced RFC 2822, which had replaced RFC 822, and it is the base that MIME builds attachments on.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5322 defines what an Internet email message looks like: header fields such as From, To, Date and Subject, then a blank line, then the body. It does not cover delivery, which SMTP handles. It replaced RFC 2822 and RFC 822, and MIME builds attachments on top of it.

tldr.problem: Mail systems from different makers had to agree on what a message looks like, apart from how it is delivered.
tldr.mechanism: A message is plain text: header fields written as Name: value, a blank line, then the body, with fixed syntax for addresses and dates.
tldr.outcome: Every mail program can parse and display any other's messages, and the same syntax is reused beyond email.

facts.label: Line length
facts.value: at most 998 characters, should be 78 or fewer

today: Every email you send or receive still uses this format. Mail clients, spam filters and libraries all parse headers according to RFC 5322, and header-based threading uses its Message-ID, In-Reply-To and References fields. The date syntax also shows up outside email, for example in HTTP and in RSS feeds.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 5322 defines the format of Internet email messages, specifying the syntax for headers and body. While SMTP (RFC 5321) handles delivery, this RFC defines what the message itself looks like.

An email message is just structured text: a set of header fields followed by a blank line and then the message body. MIME extensions add support for attachments and rich content.
sections.plainLanguage: An email message is structured text: header fields, a blank line, then the body. This RFC defines that syntax. SMTP handles delivery, and MIME extensions add attachments and rich content.

sections.title: Header Fields
sections.content:
Header fields follow the format Field-Name: Field-Value, with long values folded across multiple lines.

FromThe author(s) of the message
ToPrimary recipient(s)
CcCarbon copy recipients
BccBlind carbon copy (not visible to other recipients)
DateDate and time the message was composed
SubjectSummary of the message topic
Message-IDGlobally unique identifier for the message
In-Reply-ToMessage-ID of the message being replied to
ReferencesThread of Message-IDs for conversation tracking
sections.plainLanguage: Each header field is written as Field-Name: Field-Value, and long values can be folded across lines. Common fields are From (author), To and Cc (recipients), Bcc (hidden recipients), Date, Subject, and Message-ID (a unique identifier). In-Reply-To and References link replies into a thread.

sections.title: Address Specification
sections.content:
Email addresses can be specified in several formats:

Address Formats
Simple:      user@example.com
Display:     John Doe <john@example.com>
Group:       Team: alice@ex.com, bob@ex.com;
Quoted:      "john.doe"@example.com

The local-part (before @) is treated as case-sensitive by SMTP (RFC 5321), though most servers treat it as case-insensitive. The domain part is always case-insensitive.
sections.plainLanguage: An address can be a plain mailbox like user@example.com, a display name with the mailbox in angle brackets, a named group of addresses, or a quoted form. The part after @ is always case-insensitive. The part before it is formally case-sensitive, but most servers ignore case.

sections.title: Date and Time
sections.content:
RFC 5322 defines a specific date format used in email headers:

Date Format
date-time = [ day-of-week "," ] date time

Examples:
Wed, 04 Feb 2026 10:30:00 -0500
4 Feb 2026 15:30:00 +0000

This date format is widely used beyond email. RFC 2822 dates appear in HTTP headers, RSS feeds, and many other Internet protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: Email headers use one strict date format: an optional day of week, then date, time and time zone offset, such as Wed, 04 Feb 2026 10:30:00 -0500. The same format is also used in HTTP headers, RSS feeds and other Internet protocols.

references.text: Resnick, P., "Internet Message Format", RFC 5322, October 2008.
Freed, N. and N. Borenstein, "Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) Part One: Format of Internet Message Bodies", RFC 2045, November 1996.

data.title: A minimal RFC 5322 message
data.code:
From: Alice <alice@example.com>
To: Bob <bob@example.org>
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 10:30:00 -0500
Subject: Hello from RFC 5322
Message-ID: <unique@example.com>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain

This is the message body.
